system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.

## Question 1

Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

A.

USE: 1 Triangle Tile and
1 Trapezoid Tile
MAKE: A 4-sided figure
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

Figure, described in words:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part A response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.

output.answer_1: Use 1 triangle tile and 1 trapezoid tile to make a parallelogram. Place the trapezoid with its 2-unit base at the bottom and its 1-unit top, then attach the triangle to the outside of the right slanted side so its top edge continues the trapezoid's top edge. On the grid, draw a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 2 units and slanted sides of 1 unit, made of 4 triangle units.
output.answer_2: Use the two trapezoids to make a 6-sided concave hexagon. Place an upright trapezoid (2-unit base at the bottom, 1-unit top) on the bottom of the grid. Place an inverted trapezoid (1-unit base, 2-unit top) on top of it, sharing the 1-unit top edge of the first trapezoid. On the grid, draw the outline: bottom side 2 units, right side slanting up 1 unit, then up-right 1 unit, then a 2-unit horizontal top, then down-left 1 unit, then down-left 1 unit back to the start, with the two inner vertices pointing inward (reflex). Shade or outline the 6 triangle units used.
output.answer_3: Use the two trapezoids to make a regular hexagon. Place the upright trapezoid with its 2-unit base as a horizontal line, and place the inverted trapezoid directly below it so that their 2-unit long sides meet along the same horizontal line. On the grid, draw a regular hexagon with side length 1 unit: two horizontal sides (top and bottom), with a horizontal diagonal of length 2 units through the middle, and four slanted sides of 1 unit each. This is a convex 6-sided shape, unlike the concave hexagon in Part B.
output.answer_4: Use 2 triangle tiles and 1 trapezoid tile to make a 7-sided figure. Draw the trapezoid with a 2-unit bottom side and a 1-unit top side, and put one triangle below each of the two bottom unit segments so that each triangle points downward (their apexes hang below the base). The two triangles touch each other only at the middle point of the base. On the grid, outline the figure with 7 sides: left slant up 1 unit from the bottom-left corner, top 1 unit, right slant down 1 unit, then down-left 1 unit to the lower-right vertex, up-left 1 unit, down-left 1 unit, up-left 1 unit, and close back at the bottom-left corner. Use 5 triangle units in total.
